issues.legal_issue: A court exercising review jurisdiction over a writ judgment cannot use review to correct an alleged error on the merits or to reconsider procedural objections that do not disclose a proper ground for review.
material_facts: A writ petition challenging a settlement of part of a public road was allowed on the ground that the settlement was prohibited by the applicable land laws.

The respondents sought review, relying on two documents already in the record that had not been relied on in the parties’ affidavits, and arguing that separate writ petitions should have been filed to challenge settlements in favour of different respondents.
A successor judicial commissioner allowed the review and dismissed the writ petition.
issues.conclusion: The grounds given for allowing review were not proper grounds for review, so the judicial commissioner acted without jurisdiction. The review order was set aside and the original order allowing the writ petition was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A court exercising plenary jurisdiction under Article 226 has an inherent power of review to prevent a miscarriage of justice or correct grave and palpable errors, as recognized in Shivdev Singh v. State of Punjab. The power is limited: it may be exercised on discovery of new and important matter or evidence that, despite due diligence, was not within the applicant’s knowledge or could not have been produced earlier, on an error apparent on the face of the record, or on an analogous ground. It cannot be used to correct an alleged error on the merits, which is the province of an appellate court. The Court also held that the failure to consider documents already on the record but not relied on in the affidavits, and an objection that separate writ petitions should have been filed, did not justify review under Order 47, Rule 1 and Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

rule.if: review_of_writ_order and (overlooked_record_evidence_not_relied_on or objection_to_single_petition) and no_independent_valid_review_ground

predicates.review_of_writ_order: A party sought review of a court’s order deciding a writ petition.
predicates.overlooked_record_evidence_not_relied_on: The review applicant relied on documents already in the record that had not been relied on in the parties’ affidavits.
predicates.objection_to_single_petition: The review applicant argued that challenges concerning different respondents should have been brought in separate petitions.
predicates.no_independent_valid_review_ground: The review application rested on those grounds and did not establish another proper ground for review, such as qualifying new evidence or an apparent error.
predicates.review_order_set_aside: The court’s order allowing review is set aside.

issues.definition: When a review of a writ order rests on overlooked evidence already in the record or an objection to using a single petition, and no independent valid ground for review is established, the review order is set aside.
